headline: You can tell who someone is by the books on their shelf.
lede: So I put mine together into the shape of the person they made. Every stripe is a book, as thick as the book. Tap one to see what it gives away about me.
closing: Eleven books, one person. Still being written.

five-dysfunctions-of-a-team.line: I build trust before I build anything else, because everything else stands on it.

peopleware.line: Most technical problems are people problems in disguise, so I protect my team’s focus like it’s the product.

radical-candor.line: I’ll tell you the truth, and I’ll care how it lands. Both, every time.

drive.line: I give people room to own the work, a way to get better at it, and a reason it matters.

accelerate.line: Speed and quality go together. I measure the system instead of arguing about it.

extreme-programming-explained.line: I ship small, test early and keep the pace sustainable, for engineers and for agents.

clean-code.line: Readable work is a kindness to whoever comes next, a person or an agent.

an-elegant-puzzle.line: When a team struggles, I look for the constraint in the system before I look at a person.

the-managers-path.short: Every rung is a new job
the-managers-path.line: Engineer, manager of managers, founder: each step was a different craft, and I learned it as one.

become-an-effective-software-engineering.line: I practise leadership as everyday habits, not as a title.

the-48-laws-of-power.line: I study how politics works so I can see it coming, not so I can play it.
